props.description: Disables the master and per-app controls.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Shown when `apps` is empty. Default "No apps using audio".

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the apps table. Default "App volumes".

props.name: loading
props.description: Data is on its way. With no apps yet the card and table show placeholders; with apps the root is only marked busy.

props.name: loadingRows
props.description: Placeholder app rows while loading. Default 3.

props.name: muted
props.description: Controlled master mute state.

props.name: onAppMutedChange
props.description: Called with the app id and the new state when the user mutes or unmutes an app.

props.name: onAppVolumeChange
props.description: Called with the app id and the new volume (0 to 100) while the user moves its slider.

props.name: onDeviceChange
props.description: Called with the device id when the user picks an output device.

props.name: onMutedChange
props.description: Called with the new state when the user mutes or unmutes the output.

props.name: onVolumeChange
props.description: Called with the master volume (0 to 100) while the user moves the slider.

props.name: outputLabel
props.description: Header title. Default "Output".

props.name: volume
props.description: Master output volume 0–100.

VolumeSlider.description:
Volume control: a mute toggle (speaker icon by level), a `Slider` and the level ("64%" or "Muted").
Muting keeps the value, so unmuting restores it; moving the slider while muted unmutes.

props.name: accent
props.description: Categorical colour of the range and thumb. Default primary.

props.name: defaultMuted
props.description: Initial muted state when uncontrolled.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial volume from 0 to 100 when uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the slider and the mute button.

props.name: hideMuteButton
props.description: Hide the mute toggle (the slider alone). Default false.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name of the slider, e.g. "Music volume". Default "Volume".

props.name: levelClassName
props.description: Class for the level label.

props.name: muteButtonClassName
props.description: Class for the mute toggle, merged last (e.g. another button style).

props.name: muted
props.description:
Controlled muted state. While muted the slider keeps the stored level (turned neutral grey) unless
`zeroWhenMuted` shows it at 0. Use with `onMutedChange`.

props.name: muteLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the mute toggle. Default `Mute ${label}`.

props.name: muteToggle
props.description:
How the toggle exposes its state: `"pressed"` (default) keeps one name with `aria-pressed`;
`"label"` swaps its name between `muteLabel` and `unmuteLabel`.

props.name: onMutedChange
props.description: Called when the mute button toggles the muted state.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the new volume (0 to 100) as the slider moves.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Slider direction. Vertical stacks the toggle, slider and level in a column. Default "horizontal".

props.name: renderSlider
props.description: Wrap the slider, e.g. in a reveal-on-hover container or a popover.

props.name: restoreOnUnmute
props.description: Value to set when the toggle unmutes a level of 0 (the toggle then reads as "unmute" at 0). Default: none.

props.name: showLevel
props.description: Show the level ("64%", or "Muted") after the slider. Default true.

props.name: size
props.description: Slider and button size.

props.name: sliderClassName
props.description: Class for the slider.

props.name: step
props.description: Keyboard step. Default 1.

props.name: unmuteLabel
props.description: Accessible name of the toggle when it unmutes (`muteToggle="label"`). Default `Unmute ${label}`.

props.name: value
props.description: Volume 0–100.

props.name: zeroWhenMuted
props.description: Show the slider at 0 while muted instead of keeping the stored level. Default false.

WaterfallChart.description: Waterfall chart: floating bars that climb and fall from the running total, with totals, connectors and a signed table.

props.name: data
props.description:
One row per step. A row is a change (added to the running total; negative values fall) unless its `type` is
`"total"` (or `"subtotal"`): that bar rises from zero to its `value`, or to the running total when it has none.

props.name: animate
props.description: CSS transitions on data changes (disabled under prefers-reduced-motion). Default true.

props.name: colors
props.description: Bar colors (token names or any CSS color). Defaults: success, destructive, primary.

props.name: connectors
props.description: Dashed lines linking each bar to the next. Default true.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Content shown instead of the chart when there is no data.

props.name: grid
props.description: Horizontal gridlines. Default true.

props.name: height
props.description: Plot height in px (legend excluded). Default 260.

props.name: index
props.description: Key of the step name. Default "label".

props.name: kindLabels
props.description: Legend and table wording. Defaults "Increase", "Decrease", "Total".

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name. Defaults to a description built from the steps.

props.name: legend
props.description: Increase / decrease / total key. Default: shown below when more than one kind is present.

props.name: loading
props.description: Data is on its way: with no data, a placeholder plot (and legend) of the same size; with data, the root is marked busy.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 locale for the default number formatting. Pass one explicitly when the server and the browser must agree (SSR). Defaults to the runtime locale.

props.name: onActiveIndexChange
props.description: Called with the hovered step index (or `null` when the pointer leaves); use it to sync other views.

props.name: referenceLines
props.description: Horizontal threshold lines (`axis: "y"` only).

props.name: showValues

WheelPicker.description:
An iOS-style wheel for one list of values (time, duration, amount, day): the rows scroll with the mouse wheel or a
finger and snap one at a time (CSS scroll-snap with `scroll-snap-stop: always`, so a fling cannot skip rows), the row
in the centre is the value once the scroll stops. It is a `role="listbox"` with the selected row as
`aria-activedescendant`: Arrow keys move one row, Page keys five, Home and End jump to the ends, typing selects by
prefix, clicking a row selects it. Disabled rows are skipped. Controlled (`value`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`);
under reduced motion the keys jump instead of gliding. The accessible name comes from `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: options
props.description: Items on the wheel, as strings or `{ value, label }` objects, in order.

props.name: band
props.description: Draw the highlight band behind the centre row (a `WheelPickerGroup` draws one band across its columns). Default true.

props.description: Initially selected value when uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables scrolling and keyboard changes.

props.description: Shown when there are no options. Default "No options".

props.name: itemHeight
props.description: Row height in px. Default 36.

props.name: listClassName
props.description: Class names for the scrolling listbox.

props.name: loading
props.description: Options are on their way: placeholder rows and `aria-busy`, no listbox.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the value that is centred when scrolling settles or a key is pressed.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled selected value. Use with `onValueChange`.

props.name: visibleCount
props.description: Rows in view (odd; an even number is raised by one). Default 5.

Several wheels read as one value (hours : minutes : period, or hours and minutes of a duration) with one highlight
band across them. `value` is an array with one entry per column. Each column is a `WheelPicker`, so the keys, type-ahead
and reduced-motion behaviour are the same; the group is a labelled `role="group"`.

props.description: Called with all column values plus the column that changed.

props.name: value
props.description: One value per column, in order.

props.name: visibleCount
props.description: Rows visible per wheel (odd numbers centre the selection).

WorldMap.description:
Flat world map from bundled outlines (no network): a choropleth with a stepped legend, marker buttons (dots, icons
or avatars, optionally clustered), animated great-circle arcs, country tooltips and selection, and screen-reader tables.

props.name: arcs
props.description: Great-circle arcs between two points, for example traffic or replication links.

props.name: cluster
props.description: Merge nearby markers into count bubbles (`{ radius }` in px, default 36; 48 for compact markers).

props.name: color
props.description: Colour token or any CSS colour for the choropleth. Default `primary`.

props.name: compactMarkers
props.description: Smaller markers and a wider cluster radius. Default: on when the drawing is narrower than 480 px.

props.name: data
props.description: Choropleth values by country.

props.name: dataTable
props.description:
Render the visually hidden screen-reader tables (countries, markers, arcs). Default true. Set false when the page

props.name: defaultSelectedCountry

props.name: graticule

props.name: legend

useActiveIndicator.description:
Measures the active item of a tab strip / segmented control for a sliding indicator.
`getActive` is a selector (queried inside the container) or a function returning the element.
Re-measures when `deps` change, when the container or its items resize, and on `watchAttributes` mutations.
Items are re-collected for the resize observer whenever `deps` change, so items added later are watched too.
useActiveIndicator.signature: <T extends HTMLElement>(containerRef: RefObject<T | null>, getActive: string | ((container: T) => HTMLElement | null | undefined), deps?: DependencyList, options?: UseActiveIndicatorOptions): ActiveIndicatorState

useAddedKeys.description:
The keys that the latest change of `keys` added: empty on the first render and again after a change that only
removed or reordered. Give those items an entrance class so a list animates what is new, never what was already
there when it mounted:

  const added = useAddedKeys(values);
  <li key={v} className={added.has(v) ? "animate-pop" : undefined}>

The set stays the same until `keys` changes again, so an item keeps its class (and does not replay) across
unrelated renders. It derives the set while rendering (React's "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern), so a
new item and its class land in the same commit, and it is safe under StrictMode.

useAgentNow.description: Current time, re-rendered every `interval` ms while `active`.

useAssistantOrbState.description:
The orb state for what a voice session is doing, by priority: error, speaking, thinking, listening, muted, idle. The
assistant's own activity outranks the user's, so a barge-in shows `listening` only once the assistant stops. The result is
stable between renders for the same flags.

props.name: error
props.description: Something went wrong; wins over everything else.

props.name: listening
props.description: The microphone is open and the assistant is hearing the user.

props.name: muted
props.description: The microphone is muted; shown only when nothing else is going on.

props.name: speaking
props.description: The assistant is talking.

props.name: thinking
props.description: The assistant is working out an answer.

useAsyncAction.description:
Tracks a possibly-async action: `busy`, `error`, and a stable `run`.
Errors are caught (no unhandled rejections); results of superseded runs and after unmount are ignored.
useAsyncAction.signature: <A extends unknown[] = [], R = unknown>(fn?: ((...args: A) => R | PromiseLike<R>) | undefined, options?: UseAsyncActionOptions<Awaited<R>>): AsyncAction<A, Awaited<R>>

useAudioLevel.description: Live RMS input level (0..1) of a MediaStream, sampled each animation frame. Returns 0 without a stream.
useAudioLevel.signature: (stream: MediaStream | null | undefined, { smoothing, gain }?: { smoothing?: number | undefined; gain?: number | undefined; }): number

useBreakpoint.description: True when the viewport is at least the named breakpoint's width (`min-width`, from the tokens).

useCamera.description:
Opens a camera with getUserMedia and tracks permission and errors. Every start is guarded so a
superseded or unmounted run (StrictMode, fast toggles) releases what it acquired.

props.name: audio
props.description: Also capture audio (for recording). Default false.

props.name: constraints
props.description: Extra video constraints merged into the request (resolution, frame rate …).

props.name: deviceId
props.description: A specific camera (`exact`); takes precedence over `facingMode`.

props.name: enabled
props.description: Run the camera. When false the stream is released and the status is `"idle"`. Default true.

props.name: facingMode
props.description: Camera to ask for first (`ideal`, so a device without it still opens). Default `"environment"`.

props.name: onError
props.description: Called with the raw error when the camera can't be opened.

useCaretAnchor.description: Position a fixed popup under (or above) the caret of a field, re-measured on scroll/resize.
useCaretAnchor.signature: (ref: RefObject<HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null>, position: number | null, open: boolean): { top: number; left: number; height: number; } | null

useChangeKey.description: A counter that is 0 until `value` changes, then goes up by one per change. Use it as a `key` (and as the switch for an entrance class) to animate a value only when it changes, never on the first render: const n = useChangeKey(status); 0 ? "animate-pop" : undefined}>{icon} It derives the key while rendering (React's "adjust state when a prop changes" pattern), so the new value and its new key land in the same commit: no frame with the new value and the old key, and it is safe under StrictMode.

useChatConversation.description: Access the enclosing ChatConversation's scroll state.

useChatMessage.description: Read the enclosing message's role, variant and streaming state.

useCommandMenuShortcut.description:
Toggles a command menu with ⌘/Ctrl + `key` (default "k"). Registers in the shortcut registry when a
`ShortcutProvider` is present; otherwise uses its own listener.

useComposerHistory.description: Shell-style prompt history for composers: ↑/↓ recall previous prompts when the caret is at the start / end.
useComposerHistory.signature: ({ value, onValueChange, initialEntries, max }: UseComposerHistoryOptions): ComposerHistory

props.name: initialEntries
props.description: Seed entries, oldest first.

props.name: max
props.description: Keep at most this many entries. Default 100.

useControllableState.description:
State that can be controlled (value + onChange) or uncontrolled (defaultValue).
Functional updates compose within a tick (`set(v => v + 1)` twice adds 2) and the setter is stable.
useControllableState.signature: <T>({ value, defaultValue, onChange, }: { value?: T | undefined; defaultValue: T; onChange?: ((value: T) => void) | undefined; }): readonly [T, (next: T | ((prev: T) => T)) => void]

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value used while the state is uncontrolled.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the next value whenever it changes (controlled or not).

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled value; when it is not `undefined` the hook mirrors it and never changes it on its own.

useCopy.description: Copy text to the clipboard; `copied` flips true for `timeout` ms.
useCopy.signature: (timeout?: number): { copied: boolean; copy: (text: string) => Promise<boolean>; }

useCountdown.description: Time left until `deadline`, recomputed from the wall clock on every tick (no drift).

useDebouncedValue.description:
A copy of `value` that follows it after it has stopped changing for `delay` ms (default 300). Feed it a search box
value and fetch on the debounced one. The first render returns `value` untouched, a pending update is dropped when
the component unmounts, and a `delay` of 0 or less updates on the next tick.

useDialogs.description:
Promise-based `confirm`, `prompt` and `choose` (`if (!(await confirm("Delete?"))) return;`).
Throws when no `DialogProvider` is mounted above.

useDirection.description:
The reading direction components should assume: the nearest `DirectionProvider` with a `dir`, else the `dir` of the document
(`<html dir>`, followed live), else `"ltr"`. Pass a ref to read the nearest `dir` ancestor of that element instead (a chart
pinned to `dir="ltr"` inside an RTL page). The server renders `"ltr"` and the value settles after hydration.

useDirectoryPickerSupport.description: `supportsDirectoryPicker()` as a hook: `false` on the server and during hydration, then the real answer.

useDisclosure.description: Open/close state for any overlay or disclosure, controlled or uncontrolled, with stable handlers.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Initial open state when uncontrolled (default false).

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Called with the next state whenever it changes through `onOpen`, `onClose`, `toggle`, `setOpen` or `props`.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state.

useDrag.description:
Tracks a pointer drag: the offset follows the finger through CSS variables (no React state per move), with an axis lock,
bounds with elastic, a release velocity from a 100 ms window, `settle` with the spring maths and a click guard after a drag.
Spread `handlers` on an element, pass `ref` to it. A press that never passes `threshold` is a plain click. The pointer is
captured only once the drag starts; `pointercancel`, a lost capture and a disabled hook end it. The hook sets `touch-action`
on the element (`pan-y` for horizontal drags, `pan-x` for vertical ones, `none` for both).

props.name: allow
props.description: Asked on press; return false to ignore the whole gesture (a slider, a text field, a scrolled area).

props.name: axis
props.description: Axis that follows the finger; the other is left to native scrolling (the hook sets `touch-action`). Default "both".

props.name: bounds
props.description: Limits of the offset. A single-axis drag whose cross axis wins at the start is handed back to the page.

props.name: captureOnPress
props.description:
Relative mode: capture the pointer on the press instead of when the drag starts, and trust that the release will arrive (no
`buttons` check). For handles with nothing clickable inside, where a press is never a click (a window title bar, a resize grip).

props.name: elastic
props.description: Resistance beyond `bounds`: a 0..1 factor of the overshoot (0 = hard stop) or a curve. Default 0.

props.name: lockAxis
props.description: With `axis="both"`: decide the axis after `lockDistance` px and follow it only. Needs `touch-action: none`.

props.name: lockDistance
props.description: Distance used by `lockAxis`. Default 8.

props.name: mode
props.description:
"relative" (default): the offset is the press offset plus the pointer travel. "absolute": the offset IS the pointer position in the
track (a seek bar, a slider rail): the press itself is the first position (`onStart` then `onMove` run on it), the pointer is
captured at once, there is no threshold, axis lock, bounds or buttons check, and `touch-action` is `none`.

props.name: mouse
props.description: Also drag with the mouse (touch and pen always count). Default true.

props.name: onDown
props.description: Called on every accepted press, before any travel (stop an inertia loop here).

props.name: onEnd
props.description: Release (or `cancelled` for `pointercancel` and a lost capture): decide to commit or call `settle`.

props.name: onMove
props.description: Runs on every pointer move (pointer events are frame-aligned by the browser, so it is already once per frame).

props.name: onPosition
props.description: Runs whenever the offset changes (drag, settle frame, `set`), for consumers that write a style of their own.

props.name: rtl
props.description: Absolute mode: measure `fx` from the right edge (pass `useDirection() === "rtl"`).

props.name: scale
props.description: Relative mode: the dragged layer sits inside a parent scaled by this factor (a zoomed image), so the offset is travel / scale. Default 1.

props.name: shouldStart
props.description: Asked once when the travel passes the threshold; return false to hand the gesture back.

props.name: threshold
props.description: Pointer travel (px) before a press becomes a drag; below it taps and clicks go through. Default 4.

props.name: trackRef
props.description: Absolute mode: the element whose rectangle is the track. Default: the element the hook is bound to.

useElementSize.description: Border-box size of an element, updated on resize (`{0, 0}` until measured).

useElementWidth.description: Border-box width of an element, updated on resize (0 until measured).

useEmbedConsent.description: Read remembered embed consent (null outside an EmbedConsentProvider).

useField.description:
Wires a form control to the nearest `Field`: id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid,
disabled and required. Explicit props always win over the field context.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Extra description id(s), joined with the ids of the surrounding `Field` (description, hint, error).

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Explicit `aria-invalid`; a true value marks the control invalid.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the control; an explicit value wins over the surrounding `Field`.

props.name: id
props.description: Control id; defaults to the id of the surrounding `Field`.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Marks the control invalid; an explicit value (or a true `aria-invalid`) wins over the surrounding `Field`.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the control required; an explicit value wins over the surrounding `Field`.

useFieldContext.description: Read the surrounding field context, or `null` outside a `Field`.

useFileUpload.description: Access the nearest `FileUpload` state (files, add/remove, picker).

useFlip.description:
FLIP for a list: pass the ordered keys and put `register(key)` on each element. When the keys change (a reorder, an
insert, a removal), the elements that moved glide from their old place to the new one with WAAPI (`translate`, plus
`scale` when asked), on the motion tokens, so a style that retunes them retunes this. Positions are measured relative
to the parent, an animation still in flight is cancelled and continued from where the element is, and nothing is
measured or animated under `prefers-reduced-motion` (the list just changes) or where `animate` is missing (jsdom).
Cancels on unmount; StrictMode's second run measures the same boxes, which is no move. With `enabled` false it measures nothing.
Otherwise it measures after every render, on purpose: the "before" positions of the next change are whatever this commit laid out.

useFocusView.description: Read the focus-view state. Returns an inert "not focused" value outside a provider.

useInstallPrompt.description: Captures `beforeinstallprompt` and tracks whether the PWA is installed.

useKunjiSignIn.description: State machine for kunji sign-in: idle → loading → ready → scanned → success | expired | denied | notLinked | error.
useKunjiSignIn.signature: ({ client, onSuccess, onError, onStatusChange, autoStart, slowAfter, successDelay, pollInterval, }: UseKunjiSignInOptions): UseKunjiSignInReturn

props.name: autoStart
props.description: Start a session on mount. Default true.

props.name: onError
props.description: Called with the error when creating the session or polling fails.

props.name: onStatusChange
props.description: Called with the new status each time the attempt moves to another state.

props.name: onSuccess
props.description: Called after the success animation with the approved poll result.

props.name: pollInterval
props.description: Override the client's poll interval.

props.name: slowAfter
props.description: Mark the attempt `slow` after this many ms of loading or awaiting approval. Default 15000. 0 disables.

props.name: successDelay
props.description: Delay between the success state and `onSuccess`, for the animation. Default 900ms.

useLightbox.description: Imperative control for a `Lightbox`: `const lb = useLightbox(); lb.openAt(2); <Lightbox items={…} {...lb.props} />`.
useLightbox.signature: (initialIndex?: number): { open: boolean; index: number; openAt: (i?: number) => void; close: () => void; setIndex: Dispatch<SetStateAction<number>>; props: { open: boolean; onOpenChange: Dispatch<SetStateAction<boolean>>; index: number; onIndexChange: Dispatch<SetStateAction<number>>; }; }

useMarqueeSelection.description:
Rubber-band selection: drag on empty space inside `containerRef` to draw a rectangle and select the items it
touches. Shift-drag adds to the selection, Mod-drag (⌘ / Ctrl) toggles, a plain click on empty space clears, and
dragging near the edges scrolls the container. Presses on items or interactive elements are left alone, so item
clicks and drag-and-drop keep working.

props.name: containerRef
props.description: The scrollable (or static) element the marquee is drawn in. Give it `position: relative` to render `box`.

props.name: autoScroll
props.description: Scroll the container while dragging near its edges. `edge` is the zone in px, `speed` the max px per frame.

props.name: clearOnClick
props.description: A plain click on empty space clears the selection. Default true.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initially selected ids when uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables marquee selection.

props.name: getItemId
props.description: Reads an item's id. Default: its `data-selection-id`, else its `id`.

props.name: getItems
props.description: Supplies the items directly (wins over `itemSelector`), e.g. `files.map(f => ({ id, element: byId(id) }))`.

props.name: ignoreSelector
props.description: Extra selector for elements a drag must not start on (added to `MARQUEE_IGNORE_SELECTOR`).

props.name: itemSelector
props.description: CSS selector for selectable items inside the container. Default `[data-selection-id]`.

props.name: mode
props.description: Whether an item must touch (`intersect`, default) or lie fully inside (`contain`) the marquee.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the selected ids as the marquee changes the selection.

props.name: threshold
props.description: Pointer travel in px before a press becomes a marquee (so clicks stay clicks). Default 4.

props.name: touch
props.description: Start marquees from touch too. Off by default so touch drags keep scrolling; set `touch-action: none` when on.

props.name: value
props.description: Selected ids (controlled).

useMediaElement.description:
Subscribes to an `HTMLMediaElement` (or any `MediaElementLike`) and exposes its state plus imperative actions.
Autoplay refusals fall back to muted playback and raise `autoplayMuted`.
useMediaElement.signature: (target: MediaElementLike | RefObject<MediaElementLike | null> | RefObject<HTMLMediaElement | null> | null, options?: UseMediaElementOptions): UseMediaElementResult

useMediaPortalContainer.description: The element media menus portal into, or null for `document.body`.

useMediaQuery.description: Whether a CSS media query matches, kept in sync (SSR-safe via `useSyncExternalStore`).

useMergedRefs.description: `mergeRefs` with a stable identity while the refs themselves don't change (avoids ref churn on every render).

useNoticeQueue.description: Queue state for `RotatingNoticeBar`: dedupe by id, priority sort and a dismissed set.

useNow.description: Current time in epoch ms, re-rendering every `interval` ms while `active` (or the `fixed` time).

props.name: active
props.description: Tick only while true. Default true.

props.name: fixed
props.description: Freeze the clock at this time (tests, stories, server snapshots).

props.name: interval
props.description: Tick interval in ms. Default 1000.

useObjectUrl.description:
An object URL for a Blob or File, revoked when the source changes or the component unmounts. Returns undefined
for no source, until the URL is created, and during the first render on the server. See `useObjectUrlState`.

useObjectUrlState.description:
An object URL for a Blob or File plus a pending flag. The URL is created in an effect (StrictMode-safe), revoked
when the source changes or the component unmounts, and never returned for a source other than the current one
(so a revoked URL is never rendered). Without `URL.createObjectURL` (old runtimes, some test setups) it settles
on `url: undefined`.

useOnlineStatus.description: Tracks `navigator.onLine` with online/offline events. Renders `true` on the server and during hydration.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page (1-based).

props.name: totalPages
props.description: Total number of pages.

props.name: boundaryCount
props.description: Pages always shown at the start and end. Default 1.

props.name: siblingCount
props.description: Pages shown on each side of the current page. Default 1.

usePan.description:
Drag with inertia: a release keeps its velocity and slows down with time-based friction; past the bounds it springs back.
Built on `useDrag` (offset in `--sutra-drag-x` / `--sutra-drag-y`, no React state per move). A press stops the glide.
Under reduced motion following the finger still works but a release stops at once.
usePan.signature: ({ axis, friction, bounds, elastic, spring, onChange, mouse, enabled, allow, }?: UsePanOptions): PanBinding

props.name: elastic
props.description: Pull beyond the bounds while dragging (0..1 factor or a curve). Default 0.4.

props.name: friction
props.description: Friction per second: the speed decays as `v * exp(-friction * dt)`, so it feels the same at any frame rate. Default 6.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Runs whenever the offset changes.

props.name: spring
props.description: Spring used to settle back inside the bounds and by `to()`. Default "gentle".

usePlayerQueue.description: Queue state for a player: current item, play order and next/previous with repeat & shuffle semantics.
usePlayerQueue.signature: <T extends PlayerQueueItem>(options?: UsePlayerQueueOptions<T>): { dispatch: (action: PlayerQueueAction<T>) => PlayerQueueState<T>; current: T | null; ordered: T[]; position: number; upNext: T[]; hasNext: boolean; hasPrevious: boolean; next: (opts?: { auto?: boolean | undefined; }) => T | null; previous: (opts?: { currentTime?: number | undefined; restartAfter?: number | undefined; }) => T | null…

props.name: index
props.description: Start index in `items` (ignored when `currentId` is set). Default 0.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with the next queue state after every change.

props.name: rng
props.description: Random source for shuffling (inject for deterministic tests). Default Math.random.

usePointerVars.description:
Publishes the pointer over an element as CSS variables, for the `spotlight`, `tilt` and `magnetic` utilities. Pass the
returned ref to a box that does not itself move (tilt and magnetic go on a child, or the box would shift under the
pointer). While a mouse or pen is over it, or inside its magnetic `radius`, it sets `data-pointer="active"` and
`--px --py` (px), `--tx --ty` (-1..1) and `--pull-x --pull-y` (px), once per frame; on leave it removes them all, and
the CSS transition settles back. Touch, a primary pointer that cannot hover, and reduced motion get the resting state:
no listeners, nothing written. The effect is decoration and must not carry information.
usePointerVars.signature: <T extends HTMLElement = HTMLElement>({ radius, strength, enabled }?: UsePointerVarsOptions): RefObject<T | null>

props.name: enabled
props.description: Turn the hook off. Default true.

props.name: radius
props.description: Magnetic reach in px beyond the box. 0 (default): only while the pointer is over the element.

props.name: strength
props.description: How much of the pointer's offset from the centre the magnetic pull follows (0..1). Default 0.35.

usePrefersReducedMotion.description: Live reduced-motion preference: `<html data-motion="reduce" | "full">` wins over `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

usePresence.description:
Keeps removed items for a moment (state `"exit"`) so they can animate out, and marks new ones `"enter"`. The hook only
decides who is rendered and in which state; CSS does the motion (`data-[presence=enter]:animate-pop-in`,
`data-[presence=exit]:animate-fade-out`). Rules:
- the first render is idle for everyone (unless `initial`), so a list never animates on mount;
- a removed item stays where it was for `exitDuration`: it is kept in the same render that removes it (no one-frame
  gap), several removals keep their order, and each has its own timer, so a fast update stream cannot strand a row in
  `"exit"`; a key that comes back while exiting is a new entrance;
- under `prefers-reduced-motion` nothing enters or exits: removal is immediate and there is no `"exit"` state.
usePresence.signature: <T, K extends string | number = string>(items: readonly T[], getKey: (item: T) => K, { exitDuration, initial, holdEnter }?: UsePresenceOptions): PresenceItem<T, K>[]

usePrevious.description:
The last value that `value` had before its current one (`undefined`, or `initial`, until it first changes). It
keeps its answer across re-renders where nothing changed, so it is safe for "which way did this move" checks, and it
is derived while rendering, so it needs no effect and survives StrictMode remounts.
usePrevious.signature: <T>(value: T, initial?: T | undefined): T | undefined

useRegistryCommands.description: Registry shortcuts as runnable commands, grouped. Empty outside a `ShortcutProvider`.
useRegistryCommands.signature: ({ exclude }?: UseRegistryCommandsOptions): { groups: ShortcutRegistryGroup[]; commands: ShortcutRegistryItem[]; run: (id: string) => boolean; }

props.name: exclude
props.description: Registry ids to leave out (e.g. the palette's own toggle).

useReorder.description: Controlled/uncontrolled list state with move helpers.
useReorder.signature: <T>({ items: itemsProp, defaultItems, onItemsChange }?: UseReorderOptions<T>): { items: T[]; setItems: (next: T[] | ((prev: T[]) => T[])) => void; move: (from: number, to: number) => void; moveUp: (index: number) => void; moveDown: (index: number) => void; moveToTop: (index: number) => void; moveToBottom: (index: number) => void; }

props.name: defaultItems
props.description: Initial items when uncontrolled.

props.name: items
props.description: Controlled items in order. Use with `onItemsChange`.

props.name: onItemsChange
props.description: Called with the full list in its new order after every move.

useResizeObserver.description: Calls `callback` whenever the element resizes (no-op where `ResizeObserver` is missing).
useResizeObserver.signature: <T extends Element>(target: Target<T>, callback: (entry: ResizeObserverEntry) => void): void

useReturnFocus.description:
Hand focus back to whatever had it when a modal opened. Radix only restores focus to a `Dialog.Trigger`, so a
dialog opened from a hotkey, a `SearchTrigger` or any controlled `open` state (no trigger) drops focus to the page
body on close, which loses the user's place. Spread the returned handlers onto the Radix content; the caller's own
`onOpenAutoFocus` / `onCloseAutoFocus` run first and a `preventDefault()` in the close handler still wins. If the
opener is gone by then (a menu item that opened the dialog and unmounted), Radix's default applies.
useReturnFocus.signature: ({ onOpenAutoFocus, onCloseAutoFocus }?: AutoFocusHandlers): { onOpenAutoFocus: (event: Event) => void; onCloseAutoFocus: (event: Event) => void; }

useRollingSeries.description:
A fixed-size buffer of the most recent values, for live charts.
When `T` is itself an array, wrap single values: `push([value])`.

props.name: capacity
props.description: How many values to keep; pushing past it drops the oldest.

props.name: initial
props.description: Starting values (read on the first render; also what `reset()` restores).

useRootDirection.description:
For wrappers of Radix roots, which always write a `dir` attribute (ltr when told nothing): the direction in effect where the
root sits, read from its parent so that a provider, a `dir` container, an LTR island or `<html dir>` all win in that order.
Pass the forwarded ref in and put the returned ref on the root; pass `dir` before the consumer's props.
useRootDirection.signature: <T extends Element>(forwarded?: Ref<T> | undefined): { ref: (instance: T | null) => void | (() => VoidOrUndefinedOnly); dir: Direction; }

useSafeId.description: Stable unique id containing only `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, safe in SVG `url(#id)`, CSS selectors and `href="#id"`.

useSampler.description:
Calls `read` every `interval` ms and keeps the last `capacity` results, for live charts.
Pauses while `enabled` is false and stops on unmount. `read` may change between renders without restarting the timer.
useSampler.signature: <T = number>(read: () => T, { interval, capacity, enabled, initial, immediate }: UseSamplerOptions<T>): RollingSeries<T>

useScheduleNow.description: Re-render every `intervalMs` while `enabled`; returns the current timestamp.

useScrollable.description:
True while the element's content overflows its box. A scrolling region needs a keyboard tab stop so the arrow keys can
scroll it (WCAG 2.1.1), but one that does not overflow should not add a useless stop: give `tabIndex={scrollable ? 0 : undefined}`.
False on the server and on the first client render (so hydration matches), then measured and kept current from resizes of
the element, of its children (the content) and of the child list (content added later).

useScrollEdges.description: Scroll-edge detection for fades and prev/next buttons; updates on scroll and on resize of the container or its content.
useScrollEdges.signature: <T extends HTMLElement>(ref: RefObject<T | null>, options?: UseScrollEdgesOptions): ScrollEdges & { update: () => void; }

useScrollProgress.description:
The script fallback of the scroll-driven utilities. In browsers with `animation-timeline` the CSS does everything and
this hook does nothing (unless `always`). Elsewhere it marks the element `data-scroll="script"` and writes
`--sutra-progress` (0..1, three decimals) from the element's position, one passive scroll listener and one frame per
scroll burst; the same CSS reads the variable, whose default is 1, so an element with no script and no timeline shows
its end state. Under reduced motion it does nothing at all. Write the variable on the element you pass.

useScrollSections.description:
Scroll-spy for a list of sections: tracks which element is in view with one `IntersectionObserver`, and scrolls to
one on request (`scrollIntoView`, so a target's `scroll-margin-top` clears a fixed header). Stays on the last section
seen while none is in the observed band, never re-renders unless the active id changes, and does nothing where
`IntersectionObserver` is missing. Build your own rail on it, or use `SectionRail`.
useScrollSections.signature: ({ ids, offset, rootMargin, root, enabled, defaultActive, smooth, onActiveChange, }: UseScrollSectionsOptions): ScrollSections

props.name: ids
props.description: Element ids of the sections, in page order.

props.name: defaultActive
props.description: Active id before any section has been seen. Default the first id.

props.name: enabled
props.description: Turn tracking off (the active id then only changes through `scrollTo` and `setActive`). Default true.

props.name: offset
props.description: Pixels below the top of the scroll area where a section starts to count as current (a fixed header's height). Default 0.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Called when the active id changes, whether tracked or set.

props.name: root
props.description: The scrolling element (or a ref to it). Default: the viewport.

props.name: rootMargin
props.description: Full `IntersectionObserver` root margin, replacing the `offset` based default (`0px 0px -65% 0px`: the top third counts).

props.name: smooth
props.description: Smooth-scroll in `scrollTo`; reduced motion always jumps. Default true.

useSelectionArea.description: Selection state and item props from the nearest `SelectionArea`.

useShortcut.description: Bind `keys` to `handler`. Pass `null` keys (or `enabled: false`) to disable.
useShortcut.signature: (keys: string | string[] | null | undefined, handler: ShortcutHandler, options?: UseShortcutOptions): void

useShortcutManager.description: The nearest `ShortcutManager`, or null outside a `ShortcutProvider`.

useShortcutPlatform.description:
Platform used for `mod` and glyphs: the `platform` given to the `ShortcutProvider`, else detected. Detection is not read
during the hydrating render: the server and the first client render use the non-Mac default and a Mac browser settles on its
own platform right after hydration, so the markup never mismatches. (A client-only render detects at once.)

useShortcutRegistry.description: All labelled, non-hidden shortcuts in the registry, grouped. Deduplicated by id (latest wins).

props.name: includeInactive
props.description: Include shortcuts whose scope is not active. Default false.

useShortcuts.description: Register several shortcuts at once. Works standalone (local listener) without a provider.

useShortcutScope.description: Push a named scope while mounted so its shortcuts shadow lower scopes.

useSidebar.description: Access sidebar state. Must be used inside `SidebarProvider`.

useSlashTrigger.description: Watch a textarea for a trigger character at the start of a word and report the query under the caret.
useSlashTrigger.signature: (textareaRef: RefObject<HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null>, triggers?: readonly string[]): SlashTriggerState

useSlotContributions.description: Contributions for one slot, re-rendering when the registry changes.

useSlotRegistry.description: Access the nearest slot registry (`register`, `unregister`, `get`). Throws outside a `SlotProvider`.

useSpeechRecognition.description: Web Speech API wrapper with interim/final transcript; inert (supported=false) where unavailable.

props.name: continuous
props.description: Keep listening across pauses. Default true.

props.name: interimResults
props.description: Report partial results. Default true.

props.name: lang
props.description: BCP-47 language, e.g. "hi-IN". Default the document language.

props.name: onFinal
props.description: Called with each finalized chunk.

useSpeechSynthesis.description: speechSynthesis wrapper: voices (async-loaded), voice for `lang`, speaking state, speak/cancel.

useSpringValue.description:
A number that springs toward `target` for values CSS cannot animate (a count-up, a gauge angle, a value fed to a canvas).
Prefer CSS (`transition-spring`) for anything a transition can do. It returns the current value (one render per frame
while it moves, none at rest); with `onUpdate` it returns nothing and does not re-render. Retargeting mid-flight keeps the
velocity. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` it jumps straight to the target. The frame loop stops at rest and on unmount.
useSpringValue.signature: (target: number, options: UseSpringValueOptions & { onUpdate: (value: number) => void; }): void

useStagger.description: `stagger` with a fixed `step` (ms), as a stable function for a list: `const at = useStagger(20); style={at(i)}`.

useStickToBottom.description: Keep a scroller pinned to the bottom while content grows, until the user scrolls up.

props.name: initial
props.description: Scroll behavior for the first jump to the bottom on mount.

props.name: resize
props.description: Scroll behavior used when content grows while stuck to the bottom.

props.name: threshold
props.description: Distance in px from the bottom that still counts as "at bottom".

useStopwatch.description: Stopwatch state: elapsed ms, running flag, laps and start / pause / lap / reset actions.
useStopwatch.signature: ({ interval, autoStart }?: UseStopwatchOptions): { elapsed: number; running: boolean; laps: StopwatchLap[]; start: () => void; pause: () => void; toggle: () => void; lap: () => void; reset: () => void; }

props.name: autoStart
props.description: Starts running as soon as the hook mounts.

props.name: interval
props.description: Refresh interval while running, ms. Default 50.

useStreamingTask.description: Consume an async iterator or EventSource-like emitter of `{ progress, phase, log }` events into state.

props.name: maxLogLines
props.description: Cap on retained log lines. Default 2000.

props.name: task
props.description: Default starter used by `start()` / `retry()` when none is passed.

useSwipe.description:
Detects a flick (decided when the pointer lifts, so it never fights native scrolling).
Spread the returned handlers on an element; give it a matching `touch-action` (e.g. `touch-pan-y` for horizontal swipes).

props.name: allow
props.description: Asked on pointer down; return false to ignore the whole gesture (e.g. from inside a slider).

props.name: axis
props.description: Which axis counts. Default "both".

props.name: enabled
props.description: Turns the gesture off without unmounting; on unless set to `false`.

props.name: maxDuration
props.description: Slower gestures are reading/scrolling, not flicks. Default 750ms.

props.name: mouse
props.description: Also react to mouse drags (touch and pen always count). Default false.

props.name: onSwipe
props.description: Called after any recognised swipe, with its direction, `dx`, `dy`, duration and velocity.

props.name: onSwipeDown
props.description: Called after a downward swipe.

props.name: onSwipeLeft
props.description: Called after a swipe towards the left of the screen (not logical start).

props.name: onSwipeRight
props.description: Called after a swipe towards the right of the screen (not logical end).

props.name: onSwipeUp
props.description: Called after an upward swipe.

props.name: ratio
props.description: The winning axis must beat the other by this factor. Default 1.5.

props.name: threshold
props.description: Minimum travel in px. Default 56.

useSwipeDismiss.description:
Drag along one axis and let go: past the distance (or fast enough) it dismisses, otherwise it springs back. Built on `useDrag`,
so the offset is in `--sutra-drag-x` / `--sutra-drag-y` and nothing re-renders per move. `reset()` brings a dismissed element back.
useSwipeDismiss.signature: ({ axis, distance, velocity, onDismiss, flyOut, spring, enabled, mouse, allow, onStart, onMove, }: UseSwipeDismissOptions): DragBinding & { reset: () => void; }

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Called on a committing release with the direction (-1 left or up, 1 right or down).

props.name: distance
props.description: Release distance (px) that dismisses. Default 90.

props.name: flyOut
props.description: Fly the element off along the axis after a dismissal (it is the caller's job to remove it). Default true.

props.name: spring
props.description: The spring for the fly-out and the snap-back. Default "snappy".

props.name: velocity
props.description: Release speed (px/s) that dismisses. Default 450.

useTextareaMirror.description:
Keeps a mirror element laid out exactly like a textarea (font, padding, borders, wrapping, scrollbar gutter,
size and scroll offset) so text rendered in the mirror lines up with the textarea's glyphs.
Attach `mirrorRef` to an absolutely positioned element behind the textarea and `onScroll` to the textarea.
useTextareaMirror.signature: (textareaRef: RefObject<HTMLTextAreaElement | null>, value: string, { enabled }?: UseTextareaMirrorOptions): { mirrorRef: RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null>; sync: () => void; onScroll: () => void; }

useTheme.description:
Read and write Sutra theme attributes on <html>. `initial` seeds the theme on mount only (like `useState`);
fields it leaves out are read from <html> (`.dark`, `data-brand`, `data-neutral`, `data-radius`, `data-style`), so a theme set
before hydration is kept, then fall back to the defaults. The document is the source of truth: the value follows <html> live,
so every `useTheme` caller (and a `ThemeToggle`) sees a change made by any other, and `setTheme` writes only the fields
it is given. Only attributes that differ are written. They stay on <html> after unmount so the theme persists.
The server and hydration render the defaults (plus `initial`); the document's own theme settles right after.
useTheme.signature: (initial?: Partial<SutraTheme>): { theme: SutraTheme; setTheme: (patch: Partial<SutraTheme>) => void; }

props.name: brand
props.description: Brand palette that drives the primary colour.

props.name: mode
props.description: Colour scheme: `light` or `dark`.

props.name: neutral
props.description: Neutral palette used for backgrounds, borders and text.

props.name: radius
props.description: Corner radius preset applied to controls and cards.

props.name: style
props.description: Visual style (`data-style`). Leave it out for the stock look; `"paper"` also needs `@sutra/ui/paper.css`.

useThinkingExpandAll.description: The nearest ThinkingExpandAllProvider state, or null outside one.

useTranscriptBookmarks.description: Bookmark state helper: list, membership and toggle.
useTranscriptBookmarks.signature: (initial?: TranscriptBookmark[]): { bookmarks: TranscriptBookmark[]; setBookmarks: Dispatch<SetStateAction<TranscriptBookmark[]>>; isBookmarked: (id: string) => boolean; toggle: (entry: TranscriptBookmark) => void; remove: (id: string) => void; }

useTypewriter.description:
Types one line, or several in turn, one character at a time (graphemes are not split). A `setTimeout` chain driven by
state: one timer at a time, none once it is done, all cleared on unmount, safe under StrictMode. Under
`prefers-reduced-motion` the full text is there from the first render and nothing runs (with several lines: the first
with `loop`, otherwise the last, which is where the typing would have ended).
useTypewriter.signature: (text: string | readonly string[], options?: UseTypewriterOptions): TypewriterState

useViewTransition.description:
Returns `(update, options?) => Promise<void>` that applies a state change as a view transition: the browser
snapshots the page, React commits, and elements that share a `viewTransitionName` morph between the two states.
Use it for navigations and big swaps (list to detail, tab to tab), not for hovers or short lists (`useFlip`).
It snapshots the whole viewport and the page ignores input until it ends (a few hundred ms), so keep updates
quick. No support or reduced motion: the update just runs.

useVirtualRows.description: Fixed-height windowing: which rows of a long list are inside (or near) the viewport.
useVirtualRows.signature: ({ count, rowHeight, scrollElement, overscan, enabled, fallbackHeight, }: UseVirtualRowsOptions): VirtualRows

props.name: count
props.description: Total number of rows in the list.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: Fixed row height in px.

props.name: scrollElement
props.description: The scrolling element.

props.name: enabled
props.description: When false, every row is rendered. Default true.

props.name: fallbackHeight
props.description: Viewport height assumed before the element has been measured. Default 480.

props.name: overscan
props.description: Extra rows rendered above and below the viewport. Default 12.

useZoomPan.description:
Zoom/pan state + handlers: wheel and pinch zoom around the pointer, drag to pan, double-click reset, keyboard +/−/0/arrows.
A one-pointer pan runs on `useDrag`: the offset follows the finger through `--sutra-zoom-x/-y` on the viewport (`contentStyle`
reads them; the names are the hook's own so a nested ZoomPan or a Drawer around it never leaks an offset in), so a pan re-renders nothing; `onValueChange` still fires on every move and `state` catches up when the pan ends
(`getState()` is always live). A pinch zooms through React state as before.
